official.deadline_central_display: 6 October 2026 at 5 pm Eastern Time (2027-2028 cycle, now closed)
official.deadline_note: The 2027-2028 competition closed on 6 October 2026 and the 2028-2029 cycle is launching in Spring 2027. Campus Fulbright Program Adviser deadlines are typically earlier than the national deadline, so the effective date for most applicants is set by their own institution.
official.application_cycle: 2027-2028 award cycle - application closed 6 October 2026; 2028-2029 cycle launching Spring 2027
official.status_note: The application for the 2027-2028 Competition is now closed, with semi-finalist notification expected by the end of January 2027. The 2028-2029 award cycle application is launching in Spring 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Based on award and country, some grants may also include full or partial tuition; the Award Benefits page states this is conditional rather than universal.
benefits: 24/7 support line for urgent and non-urgent situations
12 months of non-competitive eligibility hiring status within the federal government
A stipend broadly based on the cost of living in the host country, usable for room, board and incidental costs during the grant period
For grants to Post countries: round-trip transportation to the host country and pre-departure and/or in-country orientations
For grants to Commission countries: benefits may differ significantly and are published by the relevant Fulbright Commission
Based on award and country, possible book and research allowances, mid-term enrichment activities, full or partial tuition and language study programmes
All English Teaching Assistants receive an additional 60-hour online TESOL Fundamentals Course; renewal ETAs receive a 120-hour course and 20-hour teaching practicum
eligibility: Applicants must be citizens or nationals of the United States of America at the time of the application deadline; permanent residents are not eligible
Applicants must have a conferred bachelor's degree or equivalent before the start of the grant period
Currently enrolled undergraduate or graduate degree programme students apply through their institution
U.S. citizens who are not students must hold a bachelor's degree by the award start date and not hold a PhD
Non-enrolled applicants should have relatively limited professional experience, typically 7 years or less, in the field they apply in
Applicants must meet the language requirements of the award they apply for
Applicants may hold a J.D. at the time of application
requirements: A Statement of Grant Purpose with a quality, feasible proposal aligned with the Award Description
Meet award and country specific requirements, including language requirements of the chosen award
Apply through the campus Fulbright Program Adviser and submit before the national deadline
For 2027-2028 grants, the grant must begin no later than 1 June 2028
documents: Application completed with the campus Fulbright Program Adviser
Award-specific supporting materials as listed in the relevant Award Description
selection_criteria: Project Proposal and Grant Purpose: quality and feasibility of the proposal, plan, timeline and methodology, appropriate in-country affiliation and resources, and connection between project and host country
Qualifications: academic and/or professional record, relevant training, accomplishments and extracurricular activities, and language preparation
Contribution to the Fulbright Mission: preference factors established by the Fulbright Foreign Scholarship Board and the Fulbright Commissions or Foundations
Additional factors: ability of supervising agencies abroad to arrange or confirm supervision and research clearance, and country programme requirements
It is Fulbright Foreign Scholarship Board policy that reasons for non-recommendation and non-selection are not given
coverage: Stipend broadly based on the cost of living in the host country, covering room, board and incidental costs
Round-trip transportation to the host country for grants to Post countries
Conditionally, based on award and country: book and research allowances, mid-term enrichment activities, full or partial tuition, and language study programmes
application_method: Find the Fulbright Program Adviser on your campus
Complete the online application with the adviser
Submit before the national deadline, which is typically earlier at institutional level
Applications are then screened by IIE, reviewed by National Screening Committee panels, forwarded to Posts or Commissions, and finally approved by the Fulbright Foreign Scholarship Board
official.application_route: Campus Fulbright Program Adviser first, then the online IIE application, submitted ahead of the national deadline.
official.study_mode: Full-time study, research or English teaching abroad
official.citizenship_residency: United States citizens or nationals at the time of the application deadline; permanent residents are not eligible
official.international_eligibility: No - only U.S. citizens or nationals may apply to the U.S. Student Program. Non-U.S. citizens apply to the Fulbright Foreign Student Program through the Commission or Embassy in their home country.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Award types include Study/Research Awards, English Teaching Assistant Awards, the Fulbright-National Geographic Award Program and Fulbright-Fogarty Fellowships in Public Health. Creative and Performing Arts projects fall under Study/Research and are available in all countries where Study/Research grants are offered. In some countries advanced-degree candidates are preferred and certain fields of study are not recommended.
official.research_requirement: Study/Research applications require a feasible project plan, timeline and methodology set out in the Statement of Grant Purpose, with an appropriate in-country affiliation and resources.
official.duration: One academic year or more of study, research or teaching abroad as specified in the award description; grants must traditionally correspond to the academic calendar of the host country and begin no later than 1 June 2028 for the 2027-2028 cycle
official.description: The Fulbright U.S. Student Program funds American citizens to study, conduct research, or teach English abroad, and is a programme of the U.S. Department of State with funding provided by the U.S. Government, administered by the Institute of International Education.
official.program_type: Government-funded international exchange grant administered by IIE
official.english_requirement: Applicants must meet the language requirements of the award to which they are applying and demonstrate sufficient competency to complete their project and adjust to life in the host country; award-specific language requirements are set out in each Award Description.

not_confirmed: which specific award and country a given applicant would be funded for
verification.notes: Benefits, eligibility rules, selection categories and the selection timeline were read directly from us.fulbrightonline.org. The programme publishes no stipend figure - it describes the stipend only as broadly based on the cost of living in the host country - and states that full or partial tuition applies only based on award and country, so amount fields and tuition coverage are left null.

applicant_utility.summary: The stipend is deliberately unpublished: Fulbright sets it against the cost of living in your host country, so the only way to plan is to read the Award Description for the specific country you are targeting. Because that same page decides whether tuition is covered at all, an award that looks generous in one country can be tuition-free in another, and benefits for Commission countries can differ significantly from Post countries. The national deadline of 6 October 2026 has already passed for the 2027-2028 cycle, so the realistic target is the 2028-2029 round launching in Spring 2027 - but your own campus adviser's deadline will fall months before that.
applicant_utility.best_fit: U.S. citizens without a PhD who want a year abroad and can write a specific, feasible project that connects a host country to their field.
application_readiness_checklist: Identify your campus Fulbright Program Adviser first - the application runs through them, not directly to IIE
Read the Award Description for the exact country and award type, since stipend level, tuition coverage, language requirements and whether advanced degrees are preferred vary by award
Draft the Statement of Grant Purpose around a feasible plan, timeline and methodology with a plausible in-country affiliation
Check the language requirements of the award and arrange evidence of competency early
Confirm you are not barred by the ineligibility rules - State Department or USAID employment, Fulbright Commission board or staff roles, FFSB membership, or immediate family in those categories
Check the residency rule: five or more years abroad in the six-year period preceding the national deadline makes you ineligible
common_rejection_risks: A proposal that does not align with the parameters in the Award Description, which is screened out at technical review in October
Extensive recent experience in the host country - six or more months outside undergraduate study abroad is considered extensive and recent and puts candidates at a competitive disadvantage
Having held a Fulbright grant recently: 2024-2025, 2025-2026, 2026-2027 and 2027-2028 participants are at a competitive disadvantage for the 2027-2028 competition
A baccalaureate from a non-U.S. institution, since preference goes to applicants whose higher education was undertaken primarily in the United States
Applying to the Fulbright U.S. Student Program and the Scholar Program in the same cycle, which is not allowed
Duplicative funding from another grant, which reduces Fulbright benefits
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The stipend covers room, board and incidental costs only, so visa costs, immunisations, some in-country travel beyond the grant, and any tuition not explicitly included in the award description sit with the grantee. Applicants whose projects need extensive research support, in-country travel, materials or equipment are advised to seek supplementary funding elsewhere.
document_audit: The Statement of Grant Purpose is the pivot of the whole application - reviewers rate quality and feasibility, and country-specific parameters are applied before national screening
Dual citizens must check the Award Description for the eligibility of dual nationals applying to their country of additional citizenship, since host country law may make participation infeasible
Grant timelines and start dates must be approved by the Commission or Post, so do not fix travel or enrolment around an assumed date
Applications are not decided by phone and IIE cannot predict when a specific award decision is released, so status must be tracked in the portal
alerts: The national deadline is not your deadline - campus advisers run earlier internal cut-offs, and the adviser relationship is how you enter at all

The 2027-2028 round closed 6 October 2026 with initial notification of recommended or non-recommended status by the end of January 2027 and final selections released on a rolling basis from March to June
Grant benefits are subject to federally appropriated funds, and the Department of State reserves the right to alter participating countries, award numbers, terms and allowances without notice
A finalist offer is contingent on funding availability, a suitable host placement, research clearance, medical clearance, a visa and all grant documents
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Campus Fulbright Program Adviser, online IIE application before the national deadline, October technical screening, November to December National Screening Committee review, end of January initial notification, January to April host country review, March to June rolling final decisions approved by the Fulbright Foreign Scholarship Board.
